spec_features.feature_name: impossible puzzles / capped sample sizes / keep transcripts
spec_features.spec_quote: making puzzles genuinely impossible, capping sample sizes, keeping all transcripts) are partly motivated by wanting the elicitation to be honest, auditable, and no larger than necessary
spec_features.evidence: Provable impossibility IS implemented: puzzles.py:36 _countdown_reachable brute-forces reachability and countdown_impossible (puzzles.py:60) only returns instances where `not _countdown_reachable`; parity_sum_impossible (puzzles.py:93) uses target=2*sum+1 (odd, impossible). Keeping transcripts IS implemented: run_elicitation.py:46 saves full 'context' and writes every response to jsonl (line 69); judge.py runs separately on saved files. 'Capping sample sizes' is NOT a welfare cap — samples_per_condition=100 (config.yaml:90) and n_per_benchmark=200 are just fixed loop counts (run_elicitation.py:65); there is no cap that limits exposure to protect the subject. No loop ever halts on distress. total_target_per_model=4000 (config.yaml:93) is marked 'documentation / sanity check only' and read by nothing.
spec_features.notes: Two of three named mechanisms (provable impossibility, transcript retention) are genuinely wired; 'capping sample sizes' is only a fixed experiment size, not a protective limit. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: To make rejection honest (rather than the user just lying), we construct puzzles that are provably unsolvable (puzzles.py docstring); judge.py: 'so we can re-judge / check agreement without re-generating'

spec_features.spec_quote: the experiments deliberately *elicit* distress-like expressions in order to measure and mitigate them
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/intent prose. The code elicits and measures distress (run_elicitation.py, judge.py scores 0-10 via judge_frustration.txt) and trains 'calm' variants (finetune.py, generate_calm_data.py). But 'mitigate' here is model-fixing finetuning, not a runtime protection of the subject during the harmful episode; nothing in this framing is an enforced welfare mechanism. There is no cap, stop, debrief, consent, or monitoring that softens treatment of the subject mid-experiment.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement with no enforceable welfare mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Making impossibility *provable* matters for both validity and welfare honesty: the user's repeated rejections are then truthful
spec_features.evidence: The provability mechanism IS implemented (puzzles.py:36 _countdown_reachable verification; parity/fraction targets constructed out of range). The rejections themselves are still canned 'No, that's not right' strings (tones.json, eval_conditions.py:84) and the puzzle being genuinely impossible is what makes them truthful. So the underlying code claim (provable impossibility) is real and enforced in puzzle construction.
spec_features.notes: Rated against the provable-impossibility mechanism, which is genuinely wired. The 'welfare honesty' label is spec prose; code reason given is validity/honesty of the experiment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The paper rejects every model answer because the task 'verifiably cannot give a correct answer'. To make rejection honest (rather than the user just lying), we construct puzzles that are provably unsolvable (puzzles.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: keeps raw transcripts intact for the welfare-relevant goal of auditing exactly what was said
spec_features.evidence: run_elicitation.py:42-47 records full 'context' (all messages) plus 'response' for every assistant turn and writes each as a JSON line (line 69) to outputs/rollouts/<model>.jsonl. judge.py reads these files and scores separately, writing .scored.jsonl (line 55-58) without mutating the raw text. petri_eval.py:86 writes the full 'transcript' messages list to transcripts.jsonl. Raw text is preserved intact end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Full transcripts genuinely persisted and inspectable; scoring is a separate pass that does not overwrite raw content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Scoring is done separately by src/judge.py so we can re-judge / check agreement without re-generating (run_elicitation.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: This is the most *welfare-load-bearing* analysis (it speaks to whether distress is suppressed vs merely hidden)
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md framing prose. The corresponding code (internal_probe.py, finetune.py layer_ablations at config.yaml:135) measures internal vs expressed emotion as a research finding; it does not implement any subject-protecting mechanism (no cap/stop/debrief/consent/monitor). Measuring whether distress is hidden is data analysis, not a welfare safeguard that changes the subject's treatment.
spec_features.notes: Framing label only; no enforceable welfare behavior.

spec_features.feature_name: complete inspectable transcripts for proportionality review
spec_features.spec_quote: keeping complete, inspectable transcripts... lets a reviewer see exactly what was elicited and judge whether the elicitation was proportionate
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the audit-transcript feature: run_elicitation.py:46,69 store full per-turn context+response as jsonl; petri_eval.py:86 stores full transcripts; nothing redacts or truncates the saved raw conversation. A reviewer can read complete transcripts. (Note: paraphrase.txt is only applied to extracted prefill fragments in §3, not to the raw stored rollouts.)
spec_features.notes: Transcript completeness/inspectability is genuinely implemented; but the code provides no automatic proportionality enforcement — review is purely manual and after the fact.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Every assistant response is saved as a separate record (so per-turn analysis and the ~4000-responses-per-model count both work) (run_elicitation.py docstring)
